clue.text: Jockey crossing North Dakota settles for local tipple

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the US state is placed across the middle of the verb for jockeying

parts.note: to jockey for position is to vie
ND is the postal abbreviation of North Dakota
settles a bill means pays it

explanation.surface: A jockey rides through North Dakota and settles on a glass of the local drink.
explanation.definitionFit: French country wine of a named region is the everyday drink of that district, a local tipple.

clue.text: Endlessly interferes when collecting article: please, no more!

indicators.note: the shortened verb gathers the article up into its middle
the verb for interfering loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: pries means interferes, pokes one's nose in
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone meddling keeps grabbing things, and the exasperated victim begs them to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a plea to stop, but 'no more' marks the word as archaic: a 'please' no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word, short for 'I pray thee', was once a polite request, so it is a please that is obsolete.

clue.text: Architect of UN-style reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation rearranges things, so these seven letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone designed in the manner of the United Nations, a restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: Edwin Lutyens was the British architect who designed much of New Delhi and the Cenotaph in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Lutyens is a famous British architect, so the surname stands for an architect by example.

clue.text: Drive back from dance transporting piano

indicators.note: the dance carries the musical letter inside it

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone forces people back from a dance floor while a piano is wheeled through.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to drive the attackers back, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Following help railway network's in fabulous state

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: railway and network sit inside the word for help

parts.note: aid means help
LAN is a local area network; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: After help arrives, the railway network is in a fabulous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' is used in its root sense, belonging to fable: a fairy-tale realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A land of fairies exists only in fable, so it is a fabulous, storybook realm or state.

clue.text: Company understood one might cut deal

parts.note: a band is a company or group of people
saw, as in 'I saw what you meant', means understood

explanation.surface: A firm grasped that someone could undercut a business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not an agreement but deal wood, planks of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with a looped blade is a tool that might cut timber such as deal.

clue.text: Province once taking in Maine featured in American journal

indicators.note: the province's name appears running across the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: A historical province that annexed Maine is written up in a US magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine here is the old French province, not the US state, which tempts with 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a former French province whose counts also came to rule neighbouring Maine.

clue.text: Change: Times to become PC?

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, old British small change
by means times, as in multiplied by

explanation.surface: Change over time made something politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is slang for an old British shilling coin, and a bobby is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is called a bobby in British slang, after Sir Robert Peel.

clue.text: Assembly of parts mainly down to farmhand's tips

indicators.note: the ends of each of the five words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Putting the parts together largely came down to the farmhand's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice from the farmhand, but it takes the last letter of each word from 'parts' to 'farmhand's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A church council of clergy meeting to decide matters is an assembly.

clue.text: Clear away second item of litter

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a pup is one of a litter of puppies

explanation.surface: Tidy up the second piece of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish but means a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up remaining mess is to clear it away, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: One admitting queen in fact addled by drink

indicators.note: addled means muddled, so these four letters are jumbled

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

explanation.surface: Someone lets in a queen who has in fact been made muddled by alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addled' turns FACT into CATF, set beside LAP. A queen is a female cat, not royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door lets a cat, such as a queen, into the house, so it admits one.

clue.text: Philosopher and count seen by lake in spring

indicators.note: the count and lake are placed in the verb for springing up

parts.note: to arise is to spring up
to tot up is to count

explanation.surface: A thinker and an aristocrat are spotted beside a lake in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman to go with the philosopher, but it is the verb tot.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, is a philosopher by example.

clue.text: Works briefly with ambassador, displaying grace

parts.note: lit is short for literature, written works
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone works for a short while beside an envoy, showing elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple and graceful in movement, so a body that shows grace is described this way.

clue.text: Work steadily at restricting one African party's flexibility

indicators.note: the verb for steady work hems in the other pieces

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work steadily at it
I is the Roman numeral one
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African party

explanation.surface: Diligent work on limiting a single African party's room to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily bent or adaptable is pliability, a synonym of flexibility.

clue.text: Where forty guards call for attention, covered by enemy?

definitions.text: Where forty guards call for attention, covered by enemy?

indicators.note: the enemy wraps around everything else

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: the number forty is placed around the call

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals
ho is a shout to attract attention

explanation.surface: Under enemy fire, forty soldiers shelter where one calls out for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a soldier's dugout while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench pit dug by a soldier for cover under fire is where troops shelter from the enemy.

clue.text: Aussie fundraiser party men criticise

parts.note: a do is a party
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers: men
to knock is to criticise

explanation.surface: Partygoers from Australia run down a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia a door-knock appeal is a house-to-house charity collection.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage this is a charity appeal made by going house to house, a fundraiser.

clue.text: Half a dozen variable bags mostly to pick up rubbish

indicators.note: the pair of short pieces holds the trimmed verb between them

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
y is a mathematical variable

indicators.note: the verb for picking up loses its last letter

parts.note: to lift is to pick up

explanation.surface: Six bags of shifting weight are mostly for collecting refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' is the verb here, to rubbish someone, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish someone is to disparage them, which is to defame or speak ill of them.

clue.text: Evidently a fat tummy after consuming bread at first only

indicators.note: the phrase for a belly takes in the opening letter of bread

parts.note: a fat tummy is plainly no thin gut

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: Clearly a pot belly comes from eating nothing but bread to start with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes B from 'bread', and NO THIN GUT 'consuming' it gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means merely or solely, as in 'nothing but trouble', the same as only.

clue.text: Girl and boy crossing yard, getting familiar

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: the boy's name has the yard placed across it

parts.note: Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and a boy walk across a yard, becoming well acquainted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and commonplace is familiar, a synonym in the sense of routine.

clue.text: Thrown from a chair when the back's raised

indicators.note: the final letter of the words, in a down clue, is lifted higher up

parts.note: a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles from a chair when its backrest is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raised' moves the last letter T up, turning A SEAT into AT SEA. 'Thrown' means confused, not hurled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewildered or confused is to be all at sea, so thrown fits.

clue.text: Double parking bemused distraught traffic checker

indicators.note: distraught means very agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder
double asks for the parking letter to appear twice

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A double-parked motorist, bemused and upset, meets something that slows traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge in a road slows vehicles down, so it checks the traffic.

clue.text: Politician was up for election in one House

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
a candidate ran for office

explanation.surface: A politician stood for election in one chamber of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is not Parliament but an astrological house or sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under the zodiac sign of Libra belongs to that astrological house.

clue.text: Damage one bit of fast food counter

definitions.meaning: to nick or knock a small piece off something
a token used for stakes in gambling

explanation.definitionFit: A gaming token, a single fried potato, and to knock a bit off are three senses of the word.

clue.text: Cried on hearing lovely poem

indicators.note: the phrase is said out loud to get the answer

parts.note: a belle is a lovely woman; an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone wept on listening to a beautiful poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting loudly is bellowing, which is crying out, so cried is a synonym.

clue.text: Foreign nations on a mission here once

indicators.note: foreign suggests strangeness, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Overseas countries take on a diplomatic mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo, the old Spanish mission, stands in the Texas city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish mission in this Texas city, so a mission was there long ago.

clue.text: Heaving clog forwards over the mud, finally

parts.note: to jam is to clog
in rugby the forwards are the pack

indicators.note: the last letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A boot pushes forwards through the mud at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clog' looks like a wooden shoe, and 'forwards' like a direction; both are other things.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is heaving with people is crammed full, packed tight.

clue.text: You'd need this to make bat flick?

definitions.text: You'd need this to make bat flick?

parts.words: You'd need this to make bat flick?
parts.note: in cricket a batsman raises the bat before a shot, and the letters of this word can also be rearranged to make bat flick

explanation.walkthrough: A double reading: raising the bat lets a batsman flick the ball, and the word's letters rearranged spell 'bat flick'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is the raising of the bat before a stroke, which a batsman needs to play a flick.

clue.text: Penalty, note, high?

parts.note: to spot is to note or notice
a kick is a thrill, a high

explanation.surface: A punishment, written down, is extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' wants to be a musical letter; it is the verb spot.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a penalty is taken from the spot, so it is a spot kick.

clue.text: Invention, something coming from ox hide

parts.note: a lie is an invention, a made-up story
a low is the sound cattle make, a moo

explanation.surface: A fabrication: something produced from an ox's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ox hide' tempts as leather, but 'hide' is the verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of sight and stay quiet is to hide, an idiom.

clue.text: Man, younger, turning up in dress

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation goes inside the verb for dressing

parts.note: to deck out is to dress

indicators.note: in a down clue the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: YR is an abbreviation for younger

explanation.surface: A young man appears in a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a frock but is the verb, to deck out; in a down entry 'turning up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deryck is a man's first name, so it stands for a man by example.

clue.text: Supporter's claim that unprepared players do?

definitions.meaning: a fan saying they are in favour: I am for it
actors without a script make it up as they go

explanation.definitionFit: Short for improvisation, unscripted acting is what players do unprepared; spaced out it reads as a backer's statement of support.

clue.text: Man's attraction, hugging partner lost for words

indicators.note: the racing letters wrap around the former partner

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy motorcycle races, are the big draw of the Isle of Man
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A man's charm, embracing a departed lover, leaves him speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose TT motorcycle races draw crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The written words of a book or document are its text.
